section.name: MMTP Signaling to MoQ Catalog Conversion
section.t: This section is informative: it documents how a converter that ingests an MMTP broadcast service, an ATSC 3.0 MMTP session ( Section 8.1.2.1) or an ARIB STD-B60 service, derives a MoQ catalog from the MMT signaling, and imposes no interoperability requirements on MoQ publishers or subscribers. A converter's output catalog is subject to the normative catalog requirements of Section 12.1 like any other catalog. The MP table gives the location of each Asset ( Clause 10.3.9) and the AL-FEC message the FEC parameters of each protected flow ( Annex C.6; Section 8.3 gives the fields a MoQ publisher sets, which a converter reads back).
The multicast field in the output uses the multicast endpoint format of Section 4.1. Conversion rules:

ul.li: each MMTP session the MP table locates by its source address, destination address and destination port -> one multicast.endpoints[] entry (sourceAddress, groupAddress, port), and the Assets it carries -> that endpoint's tracks[]

each Asset -> a track whose packetId is the Asset's packet_id, unique within the session ( Section 8.1.2.1.1) and carried by every packet of the flow, so a converter cannot renumber it. Section 4.1 requires each packetId value to denote one sub-flow across all endpoints of a sending entity and reserves 0 for the signaling flow, so a converter publishes sessions whose packet_ids collide under different namespaces, and never advertises a track on packet_id 0

the AL-FEC message's entry for a flow -> the track's fec object: algorithm from fec_code_id_for_repair_flow, "reed-solomon" for code point 1 and "raptorq" for 3, symbolSize (T) from length_of_repair_symbol, sourceSymbols (K) from maximum_k_for_repair_flow, repairSymbols (P) from maximum_p_for_repair_flow, and a repair track, named in fec.repairTrack, whose packetId is the packet_id that repair_flow_id names (Section 8.3). The converter accepts an entry whose number_of_assets is 1, whose coding byte is 0x14 and whose fec_code_id_for_repair_flow is 1 or 3: a source flow of several Assets ( Clause C.1) is one block sequence over the packets of several packet_ids, which no FEC instance of protects (its Section 6.3 protects one source track), a flow under any other coding structure, ssbg_mode, FFSRP_TS or FEC payload ID mode is not one that "iso-ssbg1-v1" describes ( Section 7.3), a session whose message names any other code is outside until its registry lists that code (its Section 12), and the conversion of such a flow fails. The one repair flow the one-stage entry names is the track's layer 0, and maximum_p_for_repair_flow is its P while layer 0 is the only published layer, as in a one-stage session of , whose one repair flow carries the block's whole repair count. That field bounds the repair count of a block ( Clause C.6.3: the maximum allowed number of repair symbols in a repair symbol block) where "iso-ssbg1-v1" carries P as the RSB_length of every repair packet ( Section 7.1), on which a receiver holding layer 0 fails closed when it falls below the repairSymbols its catalog holds (its Section 6.3.9), so the converter, which receives the flow's repair packets before it lists the repair track (below), fails the conversion of a flow whose repair packets carry an RSB_length below maximum_p_for_repair_flow on any block: such a flow is not one "iso-ssbg1-v1" describes. An RSB_length above the field is the append case of the next sentence. A MoQ publisher that appended a layer ( Section 6.3.9) sends the raised total in that field (Section 8.3) while the named flow carries only the P_0 symbols of each block ( Section 6.3.2), and neither the message nor the MP table describes the layers above, so the converter sets repairSymbols to maximum_p_for_repair_flow less the repairSymbols of every layer above 0 that it learns from provisioning, and one that learns none publishes the whole field, which overstates layer 0's count, and the loss tolerance a receiver derives from it, by the layers it does not list. The converter keeps the repairSymbols it first published for a track for as long as it publishes the track: a later version of the message that raises maximum_p_for_repair_flow changes nothing in its catalog, since Section 6.3.9 forbids changing the repairSymbols of a published layer while any receiver may still be consuming the source track, and says that a receiver reading the smaller bound excludes only symbols of layers it has not joined. A later version that lowers maximum_p_for_repair_flow below the total the converter first published for the track, layer 0's repairSymbols plus those of every layer above 0 it lists, is a change that section lets no publisher make, on which every receiver holding the highest layer it lists fails closed, the wire RSB_length falling below the O_i + P_i its catalog derives for that layer, which is that total, so the converter retires the source encoding and publishes the source track and its repair tracks as a separate rendition carrying the lowered value, as that section has a publisher that must retire a layer do. The conversion of a flow fails where the fec object it would yield fails a catalog rule of Sections 5.1 and 6.3.4, on which a receiver fails closed: a maximum_p_for_repair_flow of 0 names no repair flow a catalog can publish ( Section 5.1 requires a repairSymbols of at least 1 when a repair track is published), a maximum_k_for_repair_flow of 0 names no block (a sourceSymbols of at least 1), and a length_of_repair_symbol below 14 names a symbol that protects no MMTP packet under the T - 2 construction of Section 7.3, whose protected packet begins with the 12-octet MMTP packet header of Section 3.1 (a symbolSize of at least 14 under "iso-ssbg1-v1"); an entry that names code point 3 with a length_of_repair_symbol that is not a multiple of 8 names a T no "raptorq" track can carry ( Section 4.2 fixes the Symbol Alignment at 8, which an MMTP session, carrying no OTI, does not impose on its symbol length), one with maximum_k_for_repair_flow above 56403 fails rule 6 of Section 6.3.4, and one with maximum_k_for_repair_flow plus maximum_p_for_repair_flow above 2^24 names an ESI no instance can produce (rule 5, which bounds K + totalP - 1 by 2^24 - 1, a sum the two 24-bit fields can exceed); and an entry that names code point 1 with maximum_k_for_repair_flow plus maximum_p_for_repair_flow above 255 names a block no "reed-solomon" instance can hold (rule 12, which bounds K plus the repair count of every layer). The conversion also fails for a flow whose repair_flow_id is 0, the signaling flow (Section 3.1), the flow's own packet_id, or the packet_id of another track of the session, a value that Section 4.1 requires to denote one sub-flow (a repair flow carries a packet_id of its own, Clause C.6.3), and for the flows of any two entries that name one repair_flow_id or list one Asset: two source tracks naming one repair track, or two fec objects for one track, are shapes no FEC instance of has, a repair packet belonging to the instance of the track it arrived on (its Section 6.4.1). The message names the repair flow by packet_id without a location, and the MP table does not list it ( Section 5), so the converter lists the repair track in the tracks[] of each endpoint on whose session it receives packets of that packet_id, which is where a receiver without the catalog finds them; a repair-only endpoint ( Section 6.3.6) is one the converter learns from provisioning, not from the signaling

fec.interleaveDepthMs, the ISO protection-window send span from the first source or repair packet to the last: set only when the AL-FEC message's protection_window_time or an independently known source/repair send schedule supplies that span, as a positive integer millisecond upper bound that covers the complete span, never rounded down; when the span is unknown, or the message signals zero (the size-based case), the converter omits it
a live service -> isLive = true ( Section 5.2.7) on each media track and on its repair track, which the converter publishes while it ingests the service

the source composition/edit-list origin for each synchronized media track -> presentationAnchorTicks; a converter preserves one common presentation origin across audio and video, and does not emit zero merely because the source offset was unavailable
bitrate ( Section 5.2.22) from whatever signaling carries it, or from another source, or the conversion of that track fails

section.t: Flows sharing one (sourceAddress, groupAddress, port) tuple collapse into a single endpoint whose tracks[] array lists them all. MMT signaling carries no networkSource ( Section 4.2). A converter that adds an AMT network source advertises "driad" discovery only for a source address whose reverse DNS zone carries an AMT relay record, and otherwise names a relay service hostname in relay with "dns" discovery ( Section 4.2.1).

timescale, the group-duration field and mmtpMode are required fields (Section 12.1). The converter takes timescale from asset_timescale in the MP table when asset_timescale_flag is 1, and uses 90 000 Hz when that flag is 0, as specified by Clause 10.3.9.3. For each timed Asset, it obtains the presentation time of each MPU's first AU in presentation order from the PI document when PI is present; ISO/IEC 23008-1 Clause 10.5.2.1 says that the MPU timestamp descriptor is ignored in that case. Otherwise it decodes each descriptor's 64-bit NTP mpu_presentation_time value ( Clause 10.5.2) and does not treat the encoded NTP integer as a media tick count. It converts those presentation instants through the selected asset/media clock, retaining the authored media timing when NTP fractional quantization does not land on an integer media tick. That instant is not ticks (Section 4.4.1) when the MPU has leading pictures: ticks is that instant plus the difference between the authored composition times (Section 5.1) of the MPU's first AU in decode order and its earliest-presented AU, converted to the selected timescale as Section 4.4.1 requires.

The converter derives the group duration from the authored MPU/media cadence and validates it against those ticks values. It may emit groupDurationMs only when the conversion to the selected timescale is an exact positive integer tick count; when the cadence is exact only in ticks it emits groupDurationTicks. The fixed-cadence profile cannot represent a source whose MPU cadence is not one constant positive duration, so conversion fails rather than rounding or inventing a cadence. It sets mmtpMode itself. The AL-FEC message does not name fec.blockProfile, which is required for a track whose fec.algorithm is not "none" ( Section 5.1); for such a track the converter sets it to "iso-ssbg1-v1", the profile whose entry carries the coding byte 0x14 that the converter accepts (Section 8.3; Section 7.3).

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: MMT content protection uses Common Encryption (CENC) which is preserved through MoQ transport. The MMTP packet and payload headers are not encrypted by CENC, so receivers, and MMTP gateways outside MoQ, can inspect packet type, sequence, and fragmentation metadata without accessing media sample content. A MoQ relay treats the object payload, MMTP headers included, as opaque ( Section 7.8) and never parses MMTP (Section 6.2).

section.name: Multicast Security
section.t: Multicast-specific security considerations (source authentication, replay protection, AMT relay trust) are defined in Section 7.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document defines the catalog packaging value "mmtp" (Section 12.1), extending the allowed packaging values of the MOQT Streaming Format Section 5.2.4 in the same manner as . If a registry of packaging values is established for that format, this document requests registration of:
This document requests no MoQ message type registrations. FEC signaling uses no MoQ control message ( Section 5.2); no document in this suite requests a control-message codepoint.

section.name: Changes Since draft-ramadan-moq-mmt-00
section.t: This appendix is informative. It is to be removed before publication as an RFC.

ul.li: Object IDs are numbered per group: 0 for the first object of a group and one more for each later object in source order, across subgroups, as Section 6.2 requires. In -00 they restarted at 0 in each subgroup, so several objects of one group shared an Object ID, which Section 2.1 does not allow (Sections 3.1, 4.1, 4.6, 5, 5.2, and 8). Section 4.6 is retitled "Object Identifier Assignment and Reconstruction".
Section 4.1 states that an mmtp track maps one data unit, not one object, to a stream, unlike Section 6, and keeps the Group and Object numbering of its Sections 6.1 and 6.2.

The join (Section 6.1, step 3) uses the current-group join of Section 3.5: SUBSCRIBE with a Next Object LOCATION_FILTER and FILL_PARAMETERS with StartGroup = 1. Section 6.2 is now an informative note. The relay replay and completeness requirements of -00 are removed, because a publisher must not send objects outside the requested range ( Section 3.3.1).

Section 4.4.1: an mmtp publisher, whose Group numbers follow media time, does not set the DYNAMIC_GROUPS Track Property to 1, and Section 6.1 notes that NEW_GROUP_REQUEST cannot shorten a wait for the next group. A publisher that skips Group numbers on a restart signals the gap with PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP, as Section 6.1 recommends.
Section 6.1, step 1: the catalog is read through a subscription that joins its current group, as Section 5 requires, and a switching-set disagreement is handled as Section 4.4.2 specifies.

Section 4.3: objects of an mmtp track are sent in subgroups, not as datagrams. The permission for a relay to drop a subgroup under congestion is removed; Section 5.2 governs when objects go undelivered. Section 5.2.1 no longer refers to datagram paths: on a lossy path a subsample data unit completes, possibly after FEC recovery, or is discarded as incomplete, like any other data unit.

Section 4.4: a repair track carries no altGroup, so it is not a member of a switching set. In -00 it carried the altGroup of the track it protects, although its Groups are FEC blocks, not media-time-aligned Groups.

Catalog initialization data uses the initDataList and initRef fields of in place of the per-track initData field, which the current revisions of and do not define. A receiver may still accept initData from -00 implementations (Sections 4.5, 6.1, 12, and 12.1).

Switching sets (Sections 4.4 and 4.4.2): an intra-only mmtp track may use a group duration that divides that of the GOP tracks a whole number of times. The exception applies to mmtp tracks only, so cmaf members keep the Group number alignment of Section 3.2. The g * n Group mapping is the alternate mechanism of Section 4.2, and the 10^-3 tolerance only classifies a track as intra-only.

Section 4.4.2, Table 3: the optional timescale field of cmaf tracks is attributed to Section 5.2.21, not to . A loc switching-set member, like a cmaf one, carries a catalog timescale, which a TIMESCALE Property on the track must equal, so is now a normative reference. A track entry without packaging is malformed.

Section 8.3: the AL-FEC message carries in fec_code_id_for_repair_flow the Table 1 code point of the track's algorithm: 3 for "raptorq" and 1 for "reed-solomon". Sections 7 and 8.1 follow , which now fully specifies "reed-solomon" and makes it the mandatory-to-implement scheme. RaptorQ is optional there. Section 7 states that neither the MMT AL-FEC framework nor , which uses it for MMTP sessions, requires a particular code, so the codes are those specifies. is now a normative reference. The message's length_of_repair_symbol carries the track's symbolSize, which Section 12.2 reads back, and num_of_repair_symbol_per_packet is 1; its maximum_p_for_repair_flow carries the RSB_length of the track's FEC instance, the block total, which Section 12.2 reads back as repairSymbols less the layers above 0 it learns from provisioning, keeping the value it first published for a track across later versions of the message that raise the field and retiring the source encoding under one that lowers the field below the total it first published, that value plus the layers it lists ( Section 6.3.9). Section 12.2 states that the field is a bound in where "iso-ssbg1-v1" carries P as every repair packet's RSB_length, and fails the conversion of a flow whose repair packets carry an RSB_length below the field on any block. Section 8.3 sets the entry's number_of_assets to 1, the one Asset being the source track's. Section 12.2 accepts only an entry with a number_of_assets of 1, the coding byte 0x14 and code point 1 or 3, and fails the conversion of a flow whose fec object would fail a catalog rule of Sections 5.1 and 6.3.4 (a maximum K or maximum P of 0, a symbol length below 14, a RaptorQ symbol length that is not a multiple of 8, a RaptorQ maximum K above 56403 or maximum K plus maximum P above 2^24, a Reed-Solomon maximum K plus maximum P above 255), of one whose repair flow is packet_id 0, the flow's own packet_id or the packet_id of another track of the session, and of the flows of two entries that name one repair flow or list one Asset.
